newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FOUR SHARE LEAD WITH TIGER LURKING SHOT BACK AT DISNEY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FOUR SHARE LEAD WITH TIGER LURKING SHOT BACK AT DISNEY.

text.p: Four players share the lead at the Walt Disney World Classic heading into Sunday's final round, and Tiger Woods would have made it a fivesome but for a bogey on the final hole.

Jay Haas (68), Lennie Clements (66), Taylor Smith (64) and Rick Fehr (70) finished the third round at 16 under par, one stroke ahead of Woods and four others, including Payne Stewart, the 1983 Disney winner.
It is a very crowded leaderboard, with 29 players within four strokes, and all 77 players who made the cut are within eight strokes of the lead.

Despite all of the players who have a chance to win, Haas summed up the general feeling when he was asked what he would have to do Sunday to win: "One shot ahead of Tiger is probably the number to shoot for."
Woods's three-under-par 69 at the Magnolia course Saturday was a disappointing one for the 20-year-old phenomenon who has already won one tournament in his eight-week pro career.
"The only bright side is that I still have a chance to win," said Woods, lamenting several missed birdie chances.

Woods, who has shot in the 60s in 20 of the 26 rounds he has played as a pro, will qualify for next week's elite, $3 million Tour Championship if he finishes 12th or better, and simultaneously qualify for the 1997 U.S. Open by being among the top 30 money winners.
Said Woods, "the main concern is not the Tour Championship, the main concern is that I'm one shot back."

Woods's only bogey was on the last hole, a three-putt from 30 feet. He amazed everyone at the tournament by reaching the 614-yard, par-five eighth hole in two, an accomplishment that one tour pro likened to reaching the moon in two.
Said U.S. Ryder Cup player Haas, "everyone's been waiting for the next Jack Nicklaus, maybe he's here."

Of the four men Woods must pass to win for the second time in three weeks - he won the Las Vegas Invitational two weeks ago - three are veteran touring pros, and the other, Taylor Smith, is enjoying his first successful year on the tour after three failed attempts.

Scores are ordinarily extremely low at this event, but wind on Saturday really flattened the scoring. Said Haas, "I really didn't think 16-under would be good enough to lead. I was just lucky that no one really made a big run today."
